title: Count Digit Strings With Even and Prime Slots
statement:
A PIN format has n digit slots, numbered from 0 on the left. Leading zeros are allowed. The format has two rules:

  • Every slot with an even index (0, 2, 4, …) holds an even digit: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
  • Every slot with an odd index (1, 3, 5, …) holds a prime digit: 2, 3, 5 or 7.

Return how many different PINs of length n follow both rules, modulo 1 000 000 007.

examples.why: One slot, index 0, which must be even: "0", "2", "4", "6", "8". Zero counts because leading zeros are allowed.
Slots 0 and 2 have 5 choices each, slot 1 has 4: 5 · 4 · 5 = 100.
13 even slots and 12 odd slots give 5¹³ · 4¹² PINs, far more than 10⁹ + 7, so the count is reported modulo that number.

hints: The slots are independent: the choice in one slot does not limit any other. How many choices does each slot have?
There are ⌈n / 2⌉ even slots with 5 choices and ⌊n / 2⌋ odd slots with 4 choices, so the answer is 5^⌈n/2⌉ · 4^⌊n/2⌋. Multiplying n times is too slow for n = 10¹⁵.
Fast exponentiation: square the base and halve the exponent, multiplying the base into the result whenever the exponent is odd. Reduce modulo 10⁹ + 7 after every multiplication.

explain.intuition:
Each slot is chosen on its own, so the count is a product: 5 for every even slot and 4 for every odd slot. With n slots there are ⌈n / 2⌉ even ones and ⌊n / 2⌋ odd ones. The whole problem is computing 5^⌈n/2⌉ · 4^⌊n/2⌋ modulo a prime when the exponent is up to 5 · 10¹⁴.

Repeated multiplication would take 10¹⁵ steps. Fast power uses the binary form of the exponent: x¹³ = x⁸ · x⁴ · x¹, and x, x², x⁴, x⁸, … each come from squaring the previous one. That is about 50 squarings. One JavaScript trap: two numbers below 10⁹ + 7 multiply to about 10¹⁸, past the 2⁵³ limit of exact doubles, so do the modular products with BigInt.
steps: Write pow(base, exp): start with result = 1; while exp > 0, if exp is odd multiply result by base; square base; halve exp. Reduce modulo 10⁹ + 7 each time.
pitfalls: Swapping the counts: index 0 is an even slot, so for odd n there is one more 5 than 4.
Multiplying two residues as plain JavaScript numbers. The product exceeds 2⁵³ and silently loses precision.
Looping n times. It is correct but far too slow for n = 10¹⁵.

solutions.title: Multiply slot by slot
solutions.idea: Walk the n slots and multiply the running count by 5 or 4, reducing each time.

solutions.title: Fast modular power
solutions.idea: The answer is 5^⌈n/2⌉ · 4^⌊n/2⌋. Compute each power by repeated squaring in O(log n) multiplications.

followups: Write the modular multiplication without BigInt, using only 53-bit-safe numbers.
Add a rule that no two neighbouring slots may hold the same digit. How do you count now?
